title: Placement movement guard is anchored at a stale app.press — the arming chip-click's own release is measured against it
detail: The chip-arming branch never resets app.press. The arming click's release frame enters the placement branch and compares against a stale press (a previous placement press near the tray strip, or {0,0} on first arming); a release within 6px of that stale point drops a router with no fresh press.
recommended_fix: Reset app.press when arming placement (set it to the chip position or an out-of-window sentinel) so the 6px guard only measures presses made since arming.

title: mouse_tile truncates toward zero — clicks in the left letterbox margin place a router at column 0 while the right margin rejects
detail: i32() truncates toward zero: wx in (-26,0) maps to tile 0, which passes placement_valid, so an off-map click in the left margin (screen x 136-160 at 1280x720, map 1040x780, off_x=160) shows a green ghost and drops a router at column 0; the symmetric right margin (tile 40) rejects.
recommended_fix: Floor negative world coords (or reject cursors outside the map rect before validating) so both off-map margins behave symmetrically.

title: Demo `place` verb narrows i64 parse results to i32 with no range check — out-of-range positions wrap silently
detail: parse_int returns i64; i32(px) narrows unchecked, so a position like 2^32+5 wraps to an in-grid tile and the placement is silently accepted as legal instead of failing parse. spawn_node shares the pattern; the place verb is the new code.
recommended_fix: Range-check px/py against i32 bounds before the cast and return the standard parse error, matching the fail-loud style of the other verbs.

title: lower_intents appends kind-grouped, not time-ordered — a same-tick draw-before-place applies the draw against the not-yet-placed node
detail: Draws append before places regardless of at_ms, so `at 500ms place ...` + `at 500ms draw 1 3 ...` applies the draw first — .Missing_Node latches replay_error (loud, but contradicts the app's real-time order and the app-demo parity the harness promises).
recommended_fix: Append lowered commands sorted by apply_tick (stable sort), so same-tick cross-kind dependencies apply in time order like the app's fast-path.
